service.name: token-economy
service.description: Mint local tokens, grant them with server-evaluated spend rules, and settle earning and redemption between holders who share one Vrooli instance

setup.description: Build API and UI assets declared by the manifest-driven lifecycle contract

steps.name: build-api
steps.run: cd api && GOWORK=off go mod download && GOWORK=off go build -o token-economy-api .

steps.name: install-ui-deps
steps.run: if [ -f ui/package.json ]; then cd ui && (corepack pnpm install --ignore-workspace || pnpm install --ignore-workspace); else echo 'ui/ not present yet'; fi

steps.name: build-ui
steps.run: if [ -f ui/package.json ]; then cd ui && (corepack pnpm --ignore-workspace run build || pnpm --ignore-workspace run build); else echo 'ui/ not present yet'; fi

develop.description: Launch API and Vite dev server

steps.name: start-api
steps.description: Start Go API server in background

test.description: Execute phased test suite via test-genie

steps.name: check-temporal-models
steps.description: Verify formal flow artifacts via the flow-verifier scenario CLI

steps.name: run-tests
steps.description: Run all test phases via test-genie

scenario-authenticator.purpose: Holder and minter identity. A holder's view must be genuinely authenticated; a client-side role flag would make the multi-holder isolation boundary (TKE-P0-006) cosmetic.
scenario-authenticator.description: Tokens are verified locally against the published JWKS. This scenario never stores a credential and never performs a per-request authorization callback.
scenario-authenticator.degraded_behavior: Fail closed. Authenticated surfaces refuse rather than falling back to an unauthenticated view, because the isolation boundary cannot be enforced without a verifiable identity. Health reports the dependency as degraded.

notification-hub.purpose: Out-of-band relay for redemption approval requests so a minter away from the console still learns a holder is waiting.
notification-hub.description: Relay only. This scenario owns the approval queue as a first-class surface; the hub owns delivery.
notification-hub.degraded_behavior: Degrade silently. The approval queue works unchanged and no error surfaces to the holder, because the request did succeed. Only out-of-band reach is lost.

agent-manager.purpose: Verified actor provenance on journal events (TKE-P0-011), so an agent-initiated grant is distinguishable from an operator-initiated one after the fact.
agent-manager.description: Read-only verification through the shared packages/cli-core verifier. This scenario does not spawn agents and does not invent a second attribution model.
agent-manager.degraded_behavior: Degrade honestly. The event is written with the actor recorded as unverified — never promoted, never dropped, never blocking the write.
